2027-03-31.title: Wednesday of Hevoro week · Easter Wednesday
readings: Fight the good fight, having faith and a good conscience
“For mortals it is impossible, but not for God”
2027-03-31.alt: Hevoro week, the first week of the season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection). Hevoro means white: the week is kept as one great day of Easter joy. The Panchangam prints the Gospel as “Mark 10:1-7–27”; it is read here as Mark 10:17–27 (the rich man), taking the first hyphen as a typesetting break. Please verify locally.
2027-03-31.verse: For mortals it is impossible, but not for God; for God all things are possible.
theo: On this Easter Wednesday the Gospel tells of a man who “ran up and knelt before” Jesus and asked: “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?” He has kept the commandments since his youth, and Mark adds one of the tenderest lines in the Gospels: “Jesus, looking at him, loved him.” Out of that love comes the call: “You lack one thing; go, sell what you own, and give the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.” But “he was shocked and went away grieving, for he had many possessions.” Clement of Alexandria, in his little book on this passage, taught that what the Lord asks us to leave is above all the grip of wealth on the soul, the passions that make us its slaves, so that riches become a servant of love and not a master (in substance). The disciples are astonished: “Then who can be saved?” And Jesus answers: “For mortals it is impossible, but not for God; for God all things are possible.” In Easter week this sentence shines with new light. Four days ago the most impossible thing of all happened: a man who had died on a cross and been laid in a tomb rose bodily from the dead. The God who did that can also loosen the grip of possessions on a human heart.

St Paul's charge to Timothy fits the same road: “I am giving you these instructions, Timothy, my child... so that by following them you may fight the good fight, having faith and a good conscience.” Faith and conscience go together like the two oars of a boat. “By rejecting conscience, certain persons have suffered shipwreck in the faith; among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander.” Paul's severe discipline, handing them over “to Satan,” has a healing purpose: “so that they may learn not to blaspheme.” The Church corrects in order to bring back, never simply to cast out. The Second Vatican Council calls conscience the most secret core and sanctuary of a person, where one is alone with God (Gaudium et Spes 16). The rich man's conscience told him the truth when Jesus spoke; his possessions told him to walk away. Easter gives us the strength to listen to the first voice. The risen Lord, who says “Peace be with you” to his frightened disciples, also gives us his Spirit to keep our consciences clear and our faith afloat.

Hevoro week continues: keep it as Easter. Go to the Holy Qurbono if you can, and keep using the Easter greeting. This week is also a good moment to make an Easter gift of what you have, as the rich man was invited to do: give something you value to someone poor, not only something you would have thrown away. Each night before sleeping, a family can make a short examination of conscience together: where did we follow Jesus today, and where did we walk away? Then entrust everything to the God for whom all things are possible. On Sunday, New Sunday, the Church will hear how the risen Lord came through closed doors to Thomas; prepare to meet him there with your own questions.
outline: Ask: what possession would I find hardest to give up for Jesus?
Faith and a good conscience, the two oars.
Point 2 · Jesus, looking at him, loved him
The call that comes from love.
Point 3 · For God all things are possible
The impossible of Easter, and of our hearts.
live: This Easter week, give something you value to someone who is poor.
Each night this week, take two minutes as a family to ask: where did we follow Jesus today, and where did we walk away?
2027-03-31.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you looked on the rich man and loved him, and you look on us with the same love. Loosen the grip of our possessions on our hearts, and give us courage to follow you. Keep our consciences clear and our faith whole, so that we may fight the good fight to the end. You rose from the dead, for whom all things are possible: do in us what we cannot do alone. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: At the altar the Lord who gave everything, even his own Body and Blood, gives himself to us: the true treasure in heaven, already given on earth.

quick: Paul charges Timothy: fight the good fight with faith and a good conscience.
Jesus looked at the rich man and loved him, and invited him to give all and follow.
For mortals it is impossible, but not for God; for God all things are possible.
2027-03-31.action: Give something you value to someone poor today.
2027-03-31.question: What is the one thing I still lack in following Jesus?

family.explain: A man ran to Jesus and asked how to live forever with God. Jesus looked at him with love and said: give what you have to the poor and come, follow me. But the man was sad, because he had many things and did not want to let them go. Jesus loves us too, and he asks us to love him more than any of our things.
family.intention: We pray for people who have very little, and for hearts that like to share.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing each of us could share with someone this week?”

illus: A young engineer from Kollam, home for Easter, had saved for a year to buy a new phone. At the Easter Qurbono he heard the parish appeal for a family whose house had burned in the summer. On Wednesday of that week he went back to the shop, cancelled the order and took the money to the parish office in an envelope without a name. He told no one. Months later his mother found the receipt from the cancelled order in his old jacket and asked what had happened. He said only: Jesus looked at me, and I could not walk away this time.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you look on us with love. Give us hearts free enough to follow you. Amen.
share: Fight the good fight, having faith and a good conscience (1 Timothy 1:18–19). What is my good fight this Easter?
Jesus, looking at him, loved him (Mark 10:21). Do I believe that Jesus looks at me with love?
For God all things are possible (Mark 10:27). What impossible thing do I need to entrust to God?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, set our hearts free.
interc: For all who are held captive by money or possessions, that they may find the freedom of the Gospel.
For the poor, and for those who share with them in this Easter season.
For those whose faith has suffered shipwreck, that the Lord may bring them safely back.
For young people discerning how to follow Jesus, that they may not walk away from his call.
For our parish, that the joy of Easter may become generosity.
pm.close: Father, for you all things are possible: you raised your Son from the dead. Raise us from every grip that holds us, keep our faith and conscience whole, and let us follow Jesus with joy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today a man runs to Jesus, kneels and asks: good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life? (Mark 10:17). And Mark tells us: Jesus, looking at him, loved him (Mark 10:21).

Out of that love comes a hard call: go, sell what you own, and give the money to the poor... then come, follow me. The man went away grieving, for he had many possessions (Mark 10:21–22). Possessions are good, but they can take hold of the heart.

The disciples ask: then who can be saved? Jesus answers: for mortals it is impossible, but not for God; for God all things are possible (Mark 10:26–27). Four days ago we celebrated the most impossible thing of all: the Lord rose bodily from the dead. The God who did that can set our hearts free.

St Paul tells Timothy to fight the good fight, having faith and a good conscience (1 Timothy 1:18–19). This Easter week, let us give something we value to the poor, examine our conscience each night, and trust the God for whom nothing is impossible. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! A man asked Jesus how to go to heaven. Jesus looked at him with love and said: share what you have with the poor and follow me. The man went away sad because he did not want to share. But you can be different! Jesus looks at you with love too. What can you share this week with someone who has less?

On Wednesday of Hevoro week: the good fight, the look of love, and the God of the impossible.

q: The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.

sub: A man who runs and kneels.

For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

points.h: For God all things are possible
q: Is anything too wonderful for the Lord?
If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ from the dead will give life to your mortal bodies also through his Spirit that dwells in you.
points.apply: Write down one thing that seems impossible in your life and give it to God at the Holy Qurbono.

concl: The Lord looks on us with love, and calls us to a freedom we cannot reach alone.
The God who raised Jesus from the dead can do in us what is impossible for us.
2027-03-31.resolve: Keep faith and a good conscience this Easter season, share what you value, and trust the God for whom all things are possible.
